slot.brief: Read amplitude, frequency, wave speed (from ω/k) from standard-form wave equation y = A sin(ωt − kx) and identify direction of propagation; simple read-off.

stem: A travelling wave is described by $y=0.02\sin(100\pi t-2\pi x)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres and $t$ is in seconds. Which set gives its amplitude, frequency, speed and direction of propagation?

verdicts.working: From y=A sin(ωt−kx): A=0.02 m, f=ω/(2π)=50 Hz, v=ω/k=50 m s⁻¹. The minus sign indicates propagation in +x.

working:
$A=0.02$ m, $\omega=100\pi$ rad s$^{-1}$, $k=2\pi$ m$^{-1}$
$f=\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}=50$ Hz; $v=\dfrac{\omega}{k}=50$ m s$^{-1}$
$\omega t-kx$ indicates propagation in the $+x$ direction.

Independent check: From y=A sin(ωt−kx): A=0.02 m, f=ω/(2π)=50 Hz, v=ω/k=50 m s⁻¹. The minus sign indicates propagation in +x.
solution:
Comparing with $y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)$ gives $A=0.02$ m, $\omega=100\pi$ rad s$^{-1}$ and $k=2\pi$ m$^{-1}$.
$$f=\frac{\omega}{2\pi}=50\text{ Hz},\qquad v=\frac{\omega}{k}=50\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The phase $\omega t-kx$ indicates propagation in the $+x$ direction.
